title: Trespass or Burglary?
summary: Unlicensed entry, defiant trespass, peering and burglary.
note: Helps you find the right statute to read. It does not replace the statute, your prosecutor's guidance or department policy. Not yet verified against official sources.

structure.q: Did the suspect enter or hide in a structure knowing they weren't allowed to be there?
structure.help: Includes a separately secured part of a building, like a back office or apartment.

purpose.q: Was their purpose to commit an offense inside (theft, assault, damage)?
purpose.help: Purpose can be shown by tools, items taken, statements or what they did once inside.

dwelling.q: Was it a dwelling, school or school property, utility, research facility or airport secure area?

notice.q: Did they enter or stay somewhere after being told to leave, or where it was posted or fenced?
notice.help: Notice can be given in person, by signs, or by a fence or enclosure meant to keep people out.

peer.q: Did they peer into a window or opening of a home to invade someone's privacy?

points: 2nd degree if they caused, tried or threatened bodily injury, or were armed.
Charge the crime they meant to commit, or committed, separately.
Unlicensed entry into a dwelling, school or other listed place.
Unlicensed entry into any other structure.
Write down who gave notice, when, and exactly what was said, or photograph the signs.
Defense: a place open to the public where the person followed all lawful conditions.
Peering into a dwelling window or opening to invade privacy.
Note where they stood and what they could see.
Defenses include abandoned structures and places open to the public.
If they won't leave after you or the owner tell them to, it becomes defiant trespass.
